title: RID allocation "Element limit reached" error message is missing type info
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.4 onwards (specifically: introduced in 8e6ade87 / #97465), tested 4.8-dev2 - N/A: 4.3 and earlier ### System information Godot v4.8.dev2 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1047) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description The error message when `RID_Alloc` (in `rid_owner.h`) fails to allocate because of hitting the RID limit is overly generic. It just logs: ``` ERROR: Element limit reached. at: _allocate_rid (./core/templates/rid_owner.h:122) ``` (Note: I believe in-editor you get a helpful stack trace, but if I'm getting a log file from a user, it only contains the above info.) This will show the same message regardless of which type of RID has hit the limit. (Context: Each type of RID has its own `RID_Alloc` instance with its own independent limit.) It is very helpful when debugging if we could know the type of RID that was exhausted. There's an easy fix and precedent here: `RID_Alloc` actually uses `typeid` to print the element type when it shuts down and logs the number of leaked elements. We can just use the same logic to include the element type in the error message. Note that there's already a bit of an attempt to do this (it's possible to `set_description` on a `RID_Alloc` / `RID_Owner` which will change the above error message to the description, but none of the `RID_Owners` use this function anywhere in the codebase, and there are hundreds of them. Instead of manually setting the description, let's just print the element type. (I am self-assigning this as I already have a WIP PR.) ### Steps to reproduce Just cause more than about 262400* RIDs of a certain type to be allocated (note that some types, like `CanvasItem`, have higher limits, but you can do it with `Canvas`). ```gdscript for i in 262500: RenderingServer.canvas_create() ``` This logs "Element limit reached" and usually some other cryptic error (dependent on the type, but not immediately identifiable with the type) for every allocation over the limit: Ideally, the message would read "Element limit for RID of type 'Canvas' reached." \*The actual number is a few hundred higher than the limit stated in the code of 262144, because the allocator rounds up to the end of the chunk. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [rid-overflow.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30685325/rid-overflow.zip) Just run this and check the error logs.
